data.why: The repo bundles a real sample MRI volume (a Sloth bear brain scan, uint8 NIfTI) wired to the page's own 'MRI from a Sloth bear' demo button, and the same file is copied into prep/data so the browser agent can also exercise the drag-and-drop upload path with it.

goals: Drag in an MRI NIfTI volume and visually inspect it slice-by-slice in the stereotaxic viewer
Place and adjust control points to define a smoothly space-varying intensity threshold that separates brain from skull/background
Switch threshold direction (select up/down) to segment structures across different imaging contrasts (e.g., T1 vs T2)
Tune mask opacity and image brightness/contrast to visually verify the segmentation quality
Render the thresholded mask as an interactive 3D model to inspect the extracted surface
Export the resulting mask (.nii.gz) and the control points (.json) for reuse in scripted downstream workflows

review.summary: The tree states clearly what Thresholdmann is for: brain extraction with a smoothly space-varying threshold, then exporting the mask and control points for scripted reuse. Its phases, labels and cited screens hold up well. It needs small fixes before filing: add reloading control points, fix one weak screen citation in t5, add a loader feature, and split the bundled view/polarity feature.
